sc: Irritable child who drinks eagerly, sunken eyes, slow skin pinch → Some dehydration: Plan B (ORS)
Lethargic child, cannot drink, skin pinch very slow → Severe dehydration: Plan C
Bloody diarrhoea, then pallor and little urine a week later → HUS (E. coli O157)
f: Commonest: rotavirus (watery, vomiting, < 2 yr) · cholera (rice-water) · Shigella (blood, fever, convulsion) · amoeba · Campylobacter
Two signs needed · some: restless/irritable, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly, pinch slow · severe: lethargic, cannot drink, pinch very slow (> 2 s)
ORS 75 ml/kg over 4 hours · vomiting: wait 10 min, give slowly · reassess
Ringer lactate 100 ml/kg: infant 30 ml/kg in 1 h + 70 ml/kg in 5 h · child 30 in ½ h + 70 in 2½ h · no IV: ORS by NGT 20 ml/kg/h
Extra fluid · zinc 10–14 days (10 mg < 6 mo, 20 mg ≥ 6 mo) · continue feeding/breastfeeding · when to return
Dysentery: ciprofloxacin 15 mg/kg 12-hourly × 3 days · cholera: azithromycin single dose · watery diarrhoea: no antibiotic
trap: Commonest cause is viral (rotavirus), not bacterial · shock means severe dehydration · doughy skin and marked irritability → hypernatraemic dehydration · convulsion in a malnourished child → check glucose
